- Adds `_meta.json` navigation metadata and normalizes docs page titles

- Pending additional live-render/docs verification

| communication / generic | Make setup guidance actionable | partial | 6/7 | The new docs link the Sepo App install target, install issue form, and detailed install guide, and name required secrets/workflow. It does not directly link the onboarding workflow/settings pages, though this is partly reasonable for template docs. |
| coding_workflow / generic | Keep docs in sync | pass | 7/7 | The PR updates root README links, moved access-policy links, section index paths, and docs navigation metadata together with the docs restructuring. |
| coding_workflow / generic | No per-file inventory tables in docs | pass | 6/6 | The new docs index uses grouped learning/action links, not a brittle per-file inventory table. |
| coding_workflow / generic | Make surgical changes | pass | 8/8 | Changes are scoped to `.agent/docs/**`, the README pointers, and a focused docs validation test replacing the old index-link-only test. |

## Notes

- Main score drivers are positive: the PR moves the docs entry point to `.agent/docs/index.md`, adds `_meta.json` navigation metadata, updates renamed/moved links, and adds validation for no README docs pages, frontmatter titles, no leading H1 bodies, and relative link resolution.
- PR #331 context says `_meta.json` coverage validation was part of the intended test plan. The replacement test improves general docs validation, but does not yet assert that `_meta.json` page lists match markdown files. That is a useful follow-up, not a rubric-blocking issue.
- Live checks show `check` passing for PR #333.

## Findings

- **INFO:** Consider adding a focused assertion that each `_meta.json` `pages` list exactly covers the markdown pages in that folder, excluding implicit `index`. This would lock down the new navigation metadata contract described in the linked prior PR context.

## Final Rubric Verdict

PASS

## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->
<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis-head: 68886ef84a79811cb7b47ae229af8b0ff33bf1a4 -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #333 reopens the docs structure/nav metadata update from #331 after `main` was reset so it can be retested.
- It moves the docs entry point to `.agent/docs/index.md`, moves access policy under `customization/`, removes a stale workflow customization stub, and normalizes doc page titles.
- It adds `_meta.json` files as declarative navigation metadata for the docs renderer and replaces the old docs link test with broader source-level docs validation.
- The current source metadata is internally consistent, but the new validation suite does not yet enforce the new navigation metadata contract.

## Review
The PR is well-scoped and the current checks are passing. Reviewers agreed on one remaining nonblocking but actionable test coverage gap around `_meta.json` metadata.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `_meta.json` navigation metadata is not validated | WARNING | The new docs validation test checks Markdown shape and relative links, but it never parses the `_meta.json` files added by this PR. Future docs pages or section changes could drift from the declared nav while tests still pass. |

## Progress
- `check` is passing on PR #333, and reviewer verification reported `.agent && npm ci && npm test` passing with 672/672 tests.
- Current `_meta.json` files were manually/static-checked as internally consistent.
- The PR body already acknowledges pending live-render/docs verification.
- No inline comments were posted: the existing top-level rubrics review already raises the same `_meta.json` coverage gap, and there were no inline comments or review threads to update.
- The referenced external `self-evolving/repo-docs#19` could not be inspected with the available token.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>`_meta.json` navigation metadata is not validated</summary>

**Cause:** [`docs-validation.test.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/68886ef84a79811cb7b47ae229af8b0ff33bf1a4/.agent/src/__tests__/docs-validation.test.ts#L101) ends after README/frontmatter/H1/link checks and does not read the `_meta.json` files introduced as the new navigation source.

**Candidate solutions:** Add a focused subtest that walks docs folders with `_meta.json`, validates a non-empty `label`, ensures each `pages` entry resolves to an existing child Markdown file or section directory, and ensures every non-`index.md` Markdown page/section is represented exactly once.

**Comments:** The rubrics review treated this as INFO/useful follow-up, while both code reviews rated it WARNING. The issue is not blocking because current metadata is consistent, but adding the regression guard is a concrete branch change and matches the original #331 test plan.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
`FIX_PR` - The remaining issue is a small, concrete test addition that is safe for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
`MINOR_ISSUES`

## Action Items
- [ ] Add docs validation coverage for `_meta.json` labels and `pages` entries matching the actual docs files/sections.

@sepo-agent /answer what's going on with this?

This is a real but nonblocking test gap.

PR #333 adds `_meta.json` files as the new docs navigation source, e.g. root docs navigation in [`/.agent/docs/_meta.json`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/68886ef84a79811cb7b47ae229af8b0ff33bf1a4/.agent/docs/_meta.json#L1-L11) and section navigation like [`/.agent/docs/architecture/_meta.json`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/68886ef84a79811cb7b47ae229af8b0ff33bf1a4/.agent/docs/architecture/_meta.json#L1-L11). But the new docs validation test only checks README removal, frontmatter titles, leading H1s, and relative links; it stops at [`docs-validation.test.ts#L47-L101`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/68886ef84a79811cb7b47ae229af8b0ff33bf1a4/.agent/src/__tests__/docs-validation.test.ts#L47-L101) and never parses `_meta.json`.

So today, checks would still pass if someone later typoed a nav entry, forgot to add a new doc page to `_meta.json`, or left a deleted page in navigation. The current metadata appears consistent, which is why the rubrics review called it INFO/useful follow-up. The code reviewers rated it WARNING because PR #331’s own test plan explicitly called out validating `_meta.json` coverage, and this PR replaces #331.

Recommended fix is small: add one focused test in `docs-validation.test.ts` that walks folders containing `_meta.json`, validates a non-empty `label`, validates `pages` as unique string entries, ensures each entry resolves to either a child markdown file or child section directory, and ensures every non-`index.md` child markdown/section is represented exactly once. That would convert the current manual consistency check into a regression guard.

## Rubrics Update

No changes were committed to [`agent/rubrics`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/tree/agent/rubrics) from PR #333.

no rubric changes

I reviewed PR #333, its linked predecessor #331, issue comments, review comments, reviews, trusted-author signals, the diff, and existing rubrics. The only reusable-looking point was the `_meta.json` docs navigation validation gap, but it came from bot-authored review synthesis and an untrusted `CONTRIBUTOR`-associated clarification thread, with no trusted maintainer instruction to add/update rubrics.

The broader durable expectations are already covered by existing active rubrics like `keep-docs-in-sync`, `audience-first-documentation`, and `actionable-setup-guidance`, so I left the rubrics checkout unchanged.
